text:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding magnet-70k-int3 today. Quick smoke shows KV-cache divergence when we prefill a long anchored system prompt and then resume streaming. Repro attached below.

liam: Can you drop the minimal repro here? :eyes:

maya: Minimal repro (python):
```python
from redwood_client import InferClient
client = InferClient(model=\"magnet-70k-int3\")
ctx = 'SYSTEM: <long anchor> ' * 1200  # ~30k tokens
resp = client.generate(prefix=ctx + 'User: Tell me a long story about geology.')
print(resp.tokens[-5:])  # mismatch seen near token 28123
```
Output snippet: 
```
... token 28121: \"river\"
expected token 28122: \"was\"
got: \" of\"
```

sarah: That's odd — int8 baseline on same model config was clean, right?

maya: Yep. int8 and fp16 stable. int3 only. Also observation: when anchor is empty (no long prefix) the divergence doesn't appear. So it's correlated with long prefills + resume.

liam: Sounds like RoPE phase scaling interacting with prefilling offsets. Maybe the math uses local seq_len instead of global offset when computing rotary rotations on resume. Have you dumped KV indices?

maya: Quick KV dump from failing run (index, key_hash):
```
[32766] -> 0x1a3f...
[32767] -> 0x0b2c...
[0] -> 0x1a3f...  # duplicated key after wrap
[1] -> 0x9f44...
```
Note duplicate key at wrap point — looks like wrap-around collision.

eden: If the implementation uses modulo window_size for indexing but doesn't shift by global_offset this could re-use slots incorrectly when offset > window_size. Can you confirm window_size and how offset is applied?

maya: window_size=65536 in runtime. Observed duplicate at 32768 boundary not at 65536; suspicious. Possibly integer trunc/shift or half-window bug when quantized kernels run with int3 packing.

liam: Hypothesis: quantized kernel packs keys/indices into 16-bit temp, and an arithmetic overflow happens after combining pos and global_offset leading to negative wrap at half-range. Try running with env var RW_NO_QUANT_INDEXING=1 to force scalar index arithmetic.

maya: Running that now. Also kicked off CI repro: https://ci.internal/repro/4721 (will post logs).

ci-bot: CI: Repro job 4721 queued. Logs: https://ci.internal/repro/4721/logs

sarah: Parallel ask: Can you run a short bisect across two commits: (a) kernel-pack-v2 and (b) rotor-phase-normalize? One of those landed recently. If we can bisect to a commit that introduced the collision it'll help.

eden: I'll own the bisect tomorrow. Quick checklist: 1) repro with RW_NO_QUANT_INDEXING=1, 2) reproduce with -no-kv-cache, 3) dump raw rotary phase values for positions near boundary, 4) run the same prompt on int8/float32.

maya: Added a short telemetry dump command:
```bash
./bin/dump_kv --model magnet-70k-int3 --start 28090 --end 28140 > kv_slice.txt
grep -n \"duplicate\" kv_slice.txt || true
```
kv_slice.txt shows the duplicated index lines above.

liam: Also check the codepath where we convert position to rotary angle: file runtime/rotary/rotate.c line ~412 — suspected branch optimizes for small seq_len and might unsigned-cast offset incorrectly.

sarah: Assigning owners: eden -> bisect + kernel check, maya -> repro artifacts + telemetry, liam -> review rotate.c + quant pack behavior. I'll create a short ticket. :bug:

maya: Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-1428 — notes + reproducer attached.

eden: got it. Will post PR link once I have a bisect commit.

liam: If anyone hits a smoke fix (RW_NO_QUANT_INDEXING) and wants to patch quickly, we should ship a canary to Dedicated and run the long-prefill job across top 3 customer workloads.

maya: Agreed. For now, workaround documented in ticket: set RW_NO_QUANT_INDEXING=1 or use int8 build.

ci-bot: CI: Repro job 4721 finished — job status: failed (divergence reproduced). Artifacts uploaded.

sarah: Thanks all. We'll regroup after eden's bisect. :thumbsup:
